data.text: The evidence is clear. Let me record the diagnosis.

data.reason: The WAN interface's virtio (vtnet0) driver transmit path has hung — repeated "watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link flaps — so packets cannot leave the firewall even though the link shows active and the modem is registered/OPERATIONAL.

data.cause: The WAN interface's virtio (vtnet0) driver transmit path has hung — repeated "watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link flaps — so packets cannot leave the firewall even though the link shows active and the modem is registered/OPERATIONAL.
evidence: dmesg -a shows multiple 'vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0' entries interleaved with 'link state changed to DOWN/UP' cycles
ping -c 3 -n -q 198.51.100.1 fails with 'No buffer space available' (ENOBUFS) — TX queue stuck, cannot enqueue to next hop
netstat -i shows vtnet0 Oerrs=48211 (heavy output errors) while Ipkts still accumulate; interface flags still UP/RUNNING/LOWER_UP
ifconfig vtnet0 still holds a valid lease (198.51.100.27) and netstat -rn shows a working default via 198.51.100.1, so addressing/routing are fine

/var/db/wan-watchdog/state.json + events.jsonl: 4 WAN reloads during this outage all returned rc=0 yet internet stayed down, and at 03:30 the watchdog hit reload_cap (12/24h) and stopped acting — DHCP renewals do not clear the hang
modem-events/modem-metrics show cm_status OPERATIONAL and registration complete since 02:28, so the fault is on the firewall's NIC/driver, not the modem or provider
data.recommendation: Reboot gw.lan to reset the hung vtnet0 driver and its stuck transmit queue. wan_reload has already been exercised repeatedly with no effect because it only renews the DHCP lease and cannot recover a wedged NIC queue, so a full firewall reboot is required. The maintainer is away; request the reboot and let the harness decide.
